questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{2x},\,{e}^{-2}<x<1
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2{e}^{2}},$ compute $\text{E}[4{X}^{2}-2X].$

*Hint: You may assume that $\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y]$ for any random variables $X$ and $Y$ and constants $a$ and $b.$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[4{X}^{2}-2X]=4\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-2\text{E}[X]
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We already know $\text{E}[X].$ So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{{e}^{-2}}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{{e}^{-2}}^{1}\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}\,|}_{{e}^{-2}}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{4{e}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2{e}^{2}}$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{4{e}^{4}}$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4{X}^{2}-2X] & =4\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-2\text{E}[X] \\  & =4(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{4{e}^{4}})-2(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2{e}^{2}}) \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{e}^{4}}-1+\frac{1}{{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}-\frac{1}{{e}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[10-4{X}^{2}].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{2}{{x}^{2}},\,1<x<2
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[10-4{X}^{2}]=10-4\text{E}[{X}^{2}]
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}2\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=2$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[10-4{X}^{2}] & =10-4\text{E}[{X}^{2}] \\  & =10-4\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{3{x}^{2}+4}{5},\,0<x<1
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{20},$ compute $\text{E}[2X-{X}^{3}+1].$

*Hint: You may assume that $\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y]$ for any random variables $X$ and $Y$ and constants $a$ and $b.$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X-{X}^{3}+1] & =2\text{E}[X]-\text{E}[{X}^{3}]+\text{E}[1] \\  & =2\text{E}[X]-\text{E}[{X}^{3}]+1\end{aligned}
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We already know $\text{E}[X].$ So, we compute the third raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\cdot (\frac{3{x}^{2}+4}{5})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{3}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{4}{5}{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{1}{10}{x}^{6}+\frac{1}{5}{x}^{4})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{20}$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{3}]=\frac{3}{10}$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X-{X}^{3}+1] & =2\text{E}[X]-\text{E}[{X}^{3}]+1 \\  & =2\cdot \frac{11}{20}-\frac{3}{10}+1 \\  & =\frac{11}{10}-\frac{3}{10}+1 \\  & =\frac{9}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{4}(1-x),\,-2\le x\le 0.
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{3}].$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the third raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}] & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{4}(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-2}^{0}({x}^{3}-{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}){|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(0-[4+\frac{32}{5}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{52}{5}) \\  & =-\frac{13}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}, & 0\le x<1 \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{3}].$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the third raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{3}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{3}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}\,{x}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }(-\frac{1}{x}){|}_{1}^{a} \\  & =\frac{3}{16}(1-0)+{lim}_{a\to \infty }(1-\frac{1}{a}) \\  & =\frac{3}{16}+(1-0) \\  & =\frac{19}{16}\end{aligned}
$$
